name: Agent Brain — reliable agent workflow and code-aware project memory
description:
Evolve Agent Plan into a reliable, source-aware project memory in the same repository. Reuse existing requirements, single-owner Accepted Decisions, tasks, phase handoffs, context gates and atomic task ownership. Address the six reported reliability failures and then add code/rationale history, dynamic providers, graph/context, Monaco and optional Heca collaboration.

Current implementation: JSON planners under .planner; MCP/Pi can construct PlanStore directly; public v1 is read-only. The selected target is one application service per OS user managing per-project SQLite under HOME, installed under ~/.agent-plan/runtime/<version>/ (newest version starts, protocol N/N-1) and reached by the browser only on loopback, with Host/Origin checks and a pluggable authentication middleware ready for future remote strategies. Only that service opens operational databases. Pi uses its adapter; other harnesses use MCP. CLI/UI use the same authorized API. A portable repository descriptor resolves project identity independently of mutable source/worktree paths. SQLite is embedded, with no separate database service. JSON is explicit snapshot export/import, never a parallel live mirror.

Foundation sequence: P116 defines baseline/contracts; P128 separates identity, implements SQLite/documents/search, reconciles affected context and supplies the complete global service. P130 then delivers legacy migration, consistent independent backup, explicit private-Git snapshot publication/import and descriptor-based restore. These first-use capabilities do not wait for advanced target-integration analysis. Old .planner/docs/custom guidance migrate into versioned DB document folders; installed bootstrap and API content preserve discoverability and complete tool coverage.

Reliability sequence: P117 fixes one explainable ready-work selector and durable nested returns; P118 provides useful resume/context restoration; P119 applies source precedents, portable guidance and proportionate task planning. Owned work/valid returns precede ready feature -> phase -> task priority. Preserve phase context and deliberate detours; the global task queue/free-agent-pool proposal is not adopted. Read receipts prove delivery, not model understanding or retained context after compaction. The no-task guard stays warning-only.

Source/evidence sequence: P129 distinguishes attributable executions, verification at an exact source/configuration and separate per-target integration/current availability. A verified feat/two result does not appear in main because feat/one merged. P120 supplies historical/current code anchors, large-task changesets and scoped decision applicability. File:line is dated navigation, not identity. P121 discovers providers dynamically for declared/detected languages, including empty/undecided/mixed/unsupported projects; TypeScript is not a universal analyzer. P122 supplies a provenance graph and relevant context/freshness. P126 owns safe source access and compatible shared LSP; P123 supervisor inspection; P125 project-first page titles; P127 lazy editable Monaco and correct-machine external opening.

Optional P131, phase 4 right after P116/P128/P130 so a usable Heca integration ships before code intelligence, graph, LSP and Monaco, consumes Heca-Pro capabilities over a Heca-initiated restricted duplex: project-scoped rooms/members, events and room chat, with send_message as the only reverse Heca action in v1. Heca owns native host/dispatch; Heca-Pro owns rooms/roles/assignment/orchestration and wraps agent-comms in its helper. Agent Plan remains standalone, consumes the public facade and never bypasses it to contact agent-comms/models. Heca planner WebView/native hosting is external owner work. Exact DTO/route spelling and generic native layout/engine details remain owner-scoped contract choices, not released APIs.

P124 verifies standalone workflows first, then fresh installed artifacts and the optional native-Heca scope. Preserve stable UUIDs/short IDs/history and variable-width F/P/T references, derived parent states, real dependency constraints and the execution lock (in-progress / parked / abandoned with heartbeat lease and same-agent reclaim). Planner writes are not restricted between agents; every mutation records actor and requester. Every mutation reconciles affected parents/dependencies through factual updates, version-bound reviewed-unchanged evidence or durable pending obligations, with measured bounded context cost.

The complete current plan is .planner/docs/agent-brain-plan.md; decisions are in docs/agent-brain/decisions.md; technical specifications are docs/agent-brain/architecture.md, session-registration.md and heca-protocol.md. The 29 October replan replaces accumulated canonical task/phase prose while preserving the 40 existing task identities and adds one missing SQLite task. Historical registration reports are retained as dated evidence, not operational contracts.

Out of scope: multi-computer use, native transcript aggregation, a separate autonomous AgentTest product, mandatory graph/embedding/cloud service, network-authoritative team planner, per-mutation Git publication, automatic commits/PRs/releases and real user migration during planning. AgentTest remains a future producer seam for revision-bound test evidence. Preserve project/plugin goals, Guidelines and repository release governance. This registration does not start implementation or change the global feature priority.

Web UI design: The new interface is based on reviewed prototype canvases, not the current visual design. Core/service APIs own domain rules and expose consistent results to all clients. The UI handles navigation, rendering and local drafts. docs/agent-brain/ui-prototypes.md records the supplied prototype links and inspection limits; capture the reviewed design revision before implementation.

Maintained improvements and corrections: docs/agent-brain/improvements-and-fixes.md records decision-change review across prerequisites/dependents and contained tasks, useful guidance from project initialization, configurable communication/conduct, and elastic-input search for empty features/phases. Consult the register during the relevant feature/phase discovery, attach work to existing capability owners where appropriate, and update it whenever a new bug or improvement is discovered. Preserve stable entry IDs and verification evidence; the register does not replace canonical task status, priority or dependencies and does not create implementation tasks automatically.
workDone: Canonical replan registered on 2026-10-29 and finalized with the prototype/API boundary on 2026-10-30. F025, all 16 phases and 40 original task identities/history are preserved; P128/T502 is the one new SQLite/documents/search owner. All 41 tasks remain planned. Phase order, 68 task edges, 33 linked requirements and single-owner decisions are reconciled. Current execution map: .planner/docs/agent-brain-plan.md; detailed evidence: docs/agent-brain/replan-registration.md. Heca-Pro's corresponding planner reconciliation was registered on 2026-10-31: 27 open tasks amended, P011(F003)/T047 added for new-service conformance, original completed work retained. See ../heca-pro/docs/agent-brain-registration.md. No product implementation has started.
workRemaining: Implement the canonical dependency order, starting with P116 baseline and contract work. Resolve descriptor/auth/driver/import and public Heca contracts in their owners. Follow reviewed UI prototypes with business logic in core/service APIs. Heca-Pro's corresponding task contracts are reconciled; its implementation, current-service conformance T047 and native public facade T043-T046 remain open. Preserve identity/history, phase continuity, bounded context, source/native evidence and repository approval rules. No source implementation, real migration, automatic Git publication or release is authorized by registration.

acceptedDecisions.title: Evolve Agent Plan and stabilize existing workflows first
acceptedDecisions.decision: Agent Brain is an evolution in this repository. Reuse existing planner memory, requirements, decisions, tasks, checkpoints, phase handoffs and ownership. Resolve the six reported reliability problems before the code graph extensions.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user corrected the initial gap analysis: most planning/memory structures already exist; the priority is their reliable application.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Use branch feat/agent-brain from refreshed origin/main as requested. Do not create a parallel planner, forked product authority or automatic task per inventory bullet.

acceptedDecisions.title: Code intelligence targets the user project and is language independent
acceptedDecisions.decision: The analyzed code belongs to the project using Agent Plan. Persisted links and domain contracts are language independent. Resolve the declared or detected languages against extensible provider metadata and actual compatible tool capabilities, rather than a fixed language whitelist in planner core. TypeScript is the implementation host, not a universal source analyzer.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user explicitly clarified on 21 October 2026 that the previously named languages are examples, not the complete supported language set.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Use versioned provider manifests/catalog entries and user-configured compatible providers. Probe language/version/platform, workspace/build prerequisites and supplied operations before activation. A new language supported by an existing adapter is enabled through provider metadata/configuration, without editing planner core. A genuinely new protocol may need an adapter. Validate multiple unrelated language families and a dynamically added language fixture; Rust, C/C++, Java and JS/TS are non-exclusive examples. Keep coverage per provider, operation, configuration and source area; unsupported cases retain text/planning capabilities.

acceptedDecisions.title: Code links distinguish historical evidence, current location and meaning review
acceptedDecisions.decision: A file:line reference is a navigation position, not permanent identity. Preserve recoverable snapshot baselines and provenance, resolve current locations separately, and keep architectural/factual review distinct from location resolution.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user identified stale references and explanations after code changes as dangerous.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Handle dirty state and worktree/configuration identity. External rename/move/copies yield verified candidates or ambiguity; no silent semantic relinking or approved-decision rewrite.

acceptedDecisions.title: Trace large work through changesets and scoped rationale
acceptedDecisions.decision: Track an entire task changeset automatically and record significant decisions at the appropriate module/interface/function scope. Do not require manual documentation of every modified function. Prior tasks become discoverable through shared code targets even without task-to-task references.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user emphasized that tasks often implement large pieces of code and unrelated tasks later modify the same function.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Capture baseline/checkpoints/closeout and preserve initial dirty state. Attribute only observed task/session changes; ambiguous overlap remains explicit. Canonical decisions keep one durable owner and versioned history.

acceptedDecisions.title: Provide global orientation and relevant deep context
acceptedDecisions.decision: Offer a source-backed global map immediately and retrieve detailed context for the current work and its relevant impact boundaries. Do not claim that the model has instantly read or understood the entire codebase.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user asked whether a new agent receives full codebase context or only the area of work.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Retrieve applicable rules, prior rationale, correct precedents, usages/interfaces/dependencies and tests. Expose unavailable, not retrieved, stale and absent information and explicit continuation under budgets.

acceptedDecisions.title: Begin setup from discussion and declared stack, not assumed source detection
acceptedDecisions.decision: An empty folder with an undecided language is a valid project state. Record stack decisions during discussion and activate only needed analysis capabilities when their prerequisites are available. Later source detection validates declared choices.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user corrected the assumption that discussion always starts in an existing repository.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Use an extensible versioned provider catalog and explicit configured-provider entries, not a closed language enum. Resolve matching providers, reuse compatible local tools or produce a concrete preparation/configuration plan under existing installation policy, then validate real results. Protocols do not provide universal server/indexer discovery or installation. SCIP ingestion, live LSP and syntax parsing are complementary options, not three mandatory universal installations. Keep managed tools outside user application dependencies and preserve stack-undecided projects.

acceptedDecisions.title: Extend existing standards workflow with evidence rather than repeated instructions
acceptedDecisions.decision: Read and apply existing project rules and appropriate implementation precedents before writing code; preserve evidence and review final conformity. Extend the existing canonical skill/protocol instead of presenting these obligations as new functionality.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Explicit user report: agents already receive these instructions but ignore established code conventions.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Preserve project decision 7995854e-4109-48aa-b08b-a54bff4d8432 on the warning-only no-task guard. New write-denial policy is not implicitly approved. Observed reads and a checked checklist do not prove semantic conformity; document actual harness coverage and qualitative review.

acceptedDecisions.title: Keep skills portable and canonical knowledge authoritative
acceptedDecisions.decision: Use the existing canonical shared skill distribution and installed generic bootstrap for every supported harness. Pi uses its adapter; other harnesses use MCP. Project documents/custom guidance are API-delivered database content after migration, while the installed bootstrap makes those operations discoverable.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user requested generalized Agent Plan skills inspired by Everything Claude Code, usable by all agents.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: T468 synchronizes generated skills, tool wording and real lifecycle/compaction coverage. Preserve custom content and full operation parity; a DB-stored skill is not automatically discoverable. Derived graphs/search indexes remain non-authoritative and clients never receive database paths as an access contract.

acceptedDecisions.title: Keep standalone AgentTest outside this feature
acceptedDecisions.decision: Use and link existing tests and revision-bound verification evidence for Agent Brain. A separate autonomous test generation/execution product called AgentTest is not a prerequisite or an implicitly included development stream.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: AgentTest was an earlier concept, not an identified existing repository; the agreed scope prioritized the six failures and code graph.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Leave an explicit extension seam for test evidence and future integrations, and document missing coverage. Do not add a separate planner or AI testing platform under this feature.

acceptedDecisions.title: Use Monaco for the desktop source-code workspace
acceptedDecisions.decision: Use Monaco Editor for the integrated file explorer, editable source tabs, syntax coloring and diff. Source editing/saving is included. Mobile code editing is not a deciding acceptance requirement; preserve existing planner responsiveness and document actual limitations.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user selected an experience like the adjacent file explorer and clarified that mobile source editing is not a meaningful reason to prefer CodeMirror. Monaco is the resulting choice.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Load Monaco/workers/language assets on demand and ship them locally; retain the lightweight existing Markdown workflow. Choose a compatible tested integration stack and versions without assuming VS Code extension compatibility. Do not install dependencies or implement product code as part of this planning update.

acceptedDecisions.title: Share analysis through one compatible runtime owner
acceptedDecisions.decision: Agents and the editor use the same analysis service. Reuse one compatible language-server runtime for the same project/worktree, provider/version and effective configuration; the frontend does not start a duplicate process by default.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user asked whether Agent Plan and the embedded editor would run two LSP servers. The agreed architecture explicitly avoids duplication merely because both consumers exist.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Extend P121 contracts with broker-owned upstream sessions, atomic cross-host-process ownership/reuse, cancellation, consumer lifecycle and named document revisions/overlays. Monaco provider hooks call common APIs; an optional frontend LSP client/gateway must not independently initialize a competing server. Separate keys may require separate runtimes, and provider capabilities remain dynamic.

acceptedDecisions.title: Put project identity first in browser page titles
acceptedDecisions.decision: The actual project name must identify the overview and prefix entity-detail browser titles. Task detail follows ProjectName - TaskID [Short task title]; feature and phase details follow the same project-first convention.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user cannot distinguish projects when tabs show only Agent Plan or a task title. Both reported title failures must be corrected.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Use one route-aware title owner, preserve known project context through navigation/live renames/errors, retain full variable-width refs and avoid stale cleanup restoration. The bracketed description means the short entity title, not the full Markdown task description.

acceptedDecisions.title: One user-scoped application service owns HOME SQLite planners
acceptedDecisions.decision: Agent Brain persists each project in SQLite under HOME and exposes one application service per OS user for several projects. All MCP/Pi/CLI/UI consumers use its authorized API; only the service accesses operational databases. A versioned repository descriptor identifies the project. JSON is explicit portable export/import only.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user selected SQLite and descriptor-based recovery to remove worktree planner divergence, missing commits and filesystem-only discovery. This supersedes the former git-common-dir physical storage default while retaining its local clone-discovery role.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: T489 defines binding; the dedicated SQLite task owns schema/transactions/documents/search; T496 owns affected-context consistency; T490 owns global service/API/client parity. SQLite is embedded, not a separately installed database service. Driver, endpoint/auth and descriptor details are bounded implementation choices to resolve in those owners. No operational JSON mirror or implicit network authority.

acceptedDecisions.title: Planner, source workspace, caller and native runtime have separate identities
acceptedDecisions.decision: Each agent uses planner load to register its own planner session and receive context. Record native harness/session/model metadata when available, source/worktree and separate execution attempts; integrate verified Heca server/instance/workspace/member/membership/policy identities only for enrolled room agents. Delegation requires policy and separate actor/executor attribution.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: A native session ID is correlation rather than authentication, and one caller's context does not prepare another worker.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: The complete field/source/nullability contract is docs/agent-brain/session-registration.md. Shared service/dashboard lifecycle is independent of MCP sessions; no server/browser multiplication.

acceptedDecisions.title: A logical task has executions and independent target integrations
acceptedDecisions.decision: Keep one logical task with attributable execution attempts and exact-revision evidence; represent integration of produced results into each configured target separately. A verified execution does not mean code is present in the target.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: An agent can finish in a worktree while another agent merges unrelated code. A path/branch flag or single done state cannot represent that safely.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: N1/N2/N3 own the model/projections, E2 owns changeset capture. Preserve phase-scoped handoffs, dirty snapshot evidence and unknown legacy provenance. Non-code tasks do not require fabricated commits/PRs. Targets are configurable; develop/next/main release governance is unchanged.

acceptedDecisions.title: Current code availability differs from work progress and historical merges
acceptedDecisions.decision: Expose global operational progress separately from workspace/target availability and delivery. Revalidate source-dependent evidence at the selected revision; use artifact availability only for tasks that need that code, preserving global priority within ready work.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: A historical PR merge may be followed by a revert or changed implementation, and squash/rebase can change SHA identity without removing the result.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: N2 supplies bounded integration observations; N3 supplies availability and separate UI/API counters; B1 remains selector owner. Distinguish present/absent/unknown/review-required and invalidate stale evidence rather than promising general semantic equivalence.

acceptedDecisions.title: Shared-planner adoption requires lossless migration and independent recovery
acceptedDecisions.decision: Adoption stages and validates all old planner knowledge, documents and custom guidance into SQLite after immutable backup and reviewed conflicts. Activate recoverably, then publish the descriptor. Maintain consistent independent backups and complete portable export/import; missing HOME restores only from available backup/export, never an empty substitute.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Moving out of branch copies removes implicit Git distribution and exposes data loss if a clone is deleted or migration discards divergent knowledge.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: T494/T495 own legacy import, document/reference transfer, backup and explicit baseline-aware Git snapshot publication/import. The private transport leaves source checkout/index unchanged. No automatic publication per mutation, force push, mtime-wins, imported live ownership or distributed claim guarantee. Initial recovery no longer waits on T492 target integration.

acceptedDecisions.title: Every mutation reconciles affected context through bounded deltas
acceptedDecisions.decision: Task/phase/feature/project mutations and relationship changes must assess and reconcile affected ancestors and dependencies. Update only genuinely changed facts; record version-bound reviewed-unchanged or durable pending obligations. Apply a measured incremental-context budget to every F025 workflow.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user requires parent/dependency consistency without excessive token consumption. Existing instructions and timestamps alone do not ensure semantic consistency or efficient context.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: M3 (P128(F025)/T496) owns the shared impact/postcondition protocol; C2/D2/G3/B1 consume it and I1/I2 verify it. Use maintained impact indexes, expected revisions, compact receipts, effective-context-aware reuse and paginated continuation. Do not blindly rewrite ancestors, auto-revise decisions, invent edges or drop mandatory context. No new source-write denial policy or arbitrary fixed token-saving percentage is approved.

acceptedDecisions.title: Optional Heca collaboration uses a Heca-initiated restricted duplex without another orchestrator
acceptedDecisions.decision: Heca initiates the authenticated WebSocket to Agent Plan; standalone MCP/Pi callers connect independently. Every request from Agent Plan to Heca is a Heca action-catalog invocation through its single command door under a dedicated agent-plan principal role; v1 is planner reads/events for Heca plus send_message for Agent Plan. Only enrolled room agents bind to Heca; agents started manually in Heca terminals stay standalone. Agent Plan proxies the shared room chat through Heca without joining the mesh or keeping a second chat store; both UIs read and write the same conversation. Revised 2026-11-02 (docs/agent-brain/decisions.md).
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Preserve independent service lifetimes and one authority for rooms, orchestration and conversation history.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Use docs/agent-brain/decisions.md, session-registration.md and heca-protocol.md. Chat: room-visible, delivered to the orchestrator by default, @member or @all; a room without orchestrator rejects recipient-less messages; non-interrupting queue; receipts queued/sent/uncertain. Native transcript aggregation and multi-computer use are outside this delivery.

acceptedDecisions.title: Preserve phase continuity without a global task queue
acceptedDecisions.decision: Keep the existing ready feature -> phase -> task priority model after owned active work and valid pending returns. Heca orchestrators coordinate coherent phase work and approved temporary detours retain durable checkpoints and return conditions. Do not introduce the discussed global task queue, free worker pool or automatic priority-based interruption.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user deferred the queue proposal because arbitrary cross-phase dispatch increases context loss and coordination complexity.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: T462/T463/T464 own the shared contract, selection and recovery. Distinct workers can still own tasks in one phase; no new global exclusive phase lock is implied. Correct current-phase priority divergence, retain native role scope and true dependency eligibility.

acceptedDecisions.title: Prototype-led Web UI with service-owned business logic
acceptedDecisions.decision: The new Agent Plan Web UI follows reviewed prototype canvases. Domain rules, priority/eligibility, authorization, relationships and evidence interpretation belong to core and application APIs. The UI is a consumer with presentation and draft state.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: The user is redesigning the interface through prototypes. Requiring the current visual structure would contradict that design work; duplicating policies in the UI would diverge from MCP/Pi/Heca behavior.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Read docs/agent-brain/ui-prototypes.md, identify the reviewed revision and map each state/action to its owning API. Reuse suitable typed React/router/accessibility infrastructure. Prototype fixtures and badges are not evidence of live services or delivered functionality.

dependsOn: Extend completed F016/F018/F020/F021/F023/F024 behavior and preserve their current invariants.
Use existing project Guidelines, Accepted Decisions, core boundaries and verification process.
